detailed_description: Port Reference is a precision-engineered database mapping TCP/UDP port numbers to their standardized services, protocols, and operational contexts. This tool queries an authoritative dataset containing IANA-registered ports (0-65535), including well-known ports (0-1023), registered ports (1024-49151), and dynamic/private ports (49152-65535). Users can filter by protocol type (TCP/UDP/SCTP/DCCP), service name, or port range to identify associated applications, security implications, and troubleshooting contexts. It's essential for network engineers diagnosing communication failures, security analysts auditing firewall configurations, and developers debugging service conflicts. The tool's backend uses a trie data structure for O(log n) lookup performance, while the frontend provides interactive visualizations of port usage statistics. Each entry includes technical metadata like RFC references, default protocol behaviors, and common attack vectors associated with the port.
usage_steps: Access the tool via the network tools dashboard
Enter a port number in the 'Jump to Port' search bar or select 'Show All' to browse
Use the protocol filter (TCP/UDP/Both) to narrow results
Adjust the port range slider to focus on specific segments
Click column headers to sort by service name, protocol type, or port classification
Expand individual port cards to view detailed RFC documentation and security advisories
usage_examples: A system administrator identifies an unfamiliar listening port (e.g., 3389) and discovers it's associated with RDP, prompting immediate firewall rule verification
A security analyst cross-references open ports from a vulnerability scan against the tool's database to prioritize critical service exposures
A developer debugging a containerized application discovers their custom service is conflicting with the registered PostgreSQL port (5432)
A red team member validates potential SMB attack surfaces by checking for systems exposing ports 139 and 445 in unpatched configurations
